# Disk Heatmap

> Disk Heatmap is a free Windows 10/11 (x64) app that scans a drive and draws it as a nested heat map: every folder and file is a rectangle sized by the space it takes, with folders drawn inside folders. It recognizes common caches and system files, explains each in plain English with a verdict (Safe to clean, Your call, Managed by Windows), and can empty the safe ones after asking. Scanning is local; the only network request is the update check. No account, no telemetry.

Installer: https://github.com/Anuraj-dev/disk-space-heatmap/releases/latest/download/Disk-Heatmap-Setup-x64.exe (NSIS; fetches WebView2 if missing). It is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC": click More info, then Run anyway.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://anuraj-dev.github.io/disk-space-heatmap/docs/): what Disk Heatmap does, at a glance
- [Getting started](https://anuraj-dev.github.io/disk-space-heatmap/docs/getting-started.html): requirements, download, the SmartScreen prompt, install, first scan, running as administrator, uninstalling
- [Reading the map](https://anuraj-dev.github.io/disk-space-heatmap/docs/using.html): tile size, tint, heat and hatching, small items, the side panel, keys and mouse, depth, rescan
- [Cleanup rules](https://anuraj-dev.github.io/disk-space-heatmap/docs/cleanup.html): verdicts, exactly what Clean does, the Recycle Bin, and every rule with its paths
- [Troubleshooting](https://anuraj-dev.github.io/disk-space-heatmap/docs/troubleshooting.html): SmartScreen, WebView2, unreadable folders, sizes that differ from Explorer, skipped files
